To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we derive the closed-form expressions for the secrecy outage probabilities of the adaptive and the on-off transmission schemes, and that the adaptive transmission scheme achieves the maximum effective secrecy throughputs while incurring lower secrecy outage probability.

we have developed two transmission schemes for the multi-input single-output (MISO) wiretap channel that are able to maximize the effective secrecy throughput, while incurring a low secrecy outage probability, by optimally allocating the power between the information signal, the AN, and the secrecy rate for the on-off transmission and adaptive transmission schemes.

we derive closed-form expressions for outage probabilities and secrecy outage probabilities in the on-off transmission case and the adaptive transmission case, and we determine the optimal secrecy rates and the optimal power allocation for the information signal and artificial noise signal for both transmission schemes to maximize the effective secrecy throughput.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of artificial noise (or jamming) in multi-input-single-output wiretap channels to improve the effective secrecy throughput while minimizing the secrecy outage probability.
the design and analysis of the optimal AN transmission scheme in a multi-input single-output wireless wiretap channel.
a novel approach of using AN to improve the secrecy performance in wireless communications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed transmission scheme with adaptive transmission achieves the highest effective secrecy throughput while the on-off transmission achieves the highest secrecy outage performance.
we have shown that the optimal power allocation for artificial noise is not a trivial problem.
the adaptive transmission scheme is more efficient than the on-off transmission one in terms of the secrecy outage probability and the maximum effective secrecy rate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a framework to evaluate and optimize the secrecy rate of AN transmission schemes in multi-input singleoutput wiretap channels.
we have proposed two transmission schemes for the multi-input single-output Gaussian wiretap channel and have optimized the secrecy performance of the proposed schemes.
we have proposed two novel schemes for the artificial noise in multi- input single-output wiretap channel and have derived closed-form expressions for the secrecy performance of both schemes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the secrecy performance of AN is improved by using a proper power allocation between the AN and the information signals.
the use of AN can significantly improve the secrecy performance of multi-input single-output systems.
the optimal power allocation and the optimal secrecy rate depend on the quality of the channel, which is unknown at the transmitter.
